examples.knowledge_point: Solving a Trigonometric Equation Involving Tangent Under a Modified Domain
examples.problem: Solve the equation $3 \tan x - \sqrt{3} = 0$ for $-180^\circ < x \leq 180^\circ.$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation, isolating $\tan x \mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{tan}⁡x-\sqrt{3} & =0 \\ 3\operatorname{tan}⁡x & =\sqrt{3} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡x & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3})={30}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $30^\circ$ lies inside the given domain, our first solution is $x_1 =30^\circ.$

To generate more solutions, we subtract integer multiples of $180^\circ$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-{180}^{∘} \\  & ={30}^{∘}-{180}^{∘} \\  & =-{150}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solutions are $x=-150^\circ, 30^\circ.$

feedback.problem: Solve the equation $3\operatorname{tan}⁡x-33=0$ for ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘},$ rounded to the nearest integer.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation and isolate $\operatorname{tan}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{tan}⁡x-33=0 \\ 3\operatorname{tan}⁡x & =33 \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡x & =11\end{aligned}
$$

Next,  we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(11)=84.805\,571{…}^{∘}≈{84.81}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${84.81}^{∘}$ lies inside the given domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}={84.81}^{∘}.$

To generate more solutions, we add integer multiples of ${180}^{∘}.$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}={180}^{∘}+{84.81}^{∘}={264.81}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solutions are

$$
x={85}^{∘},{265}^{∘}
$$

rounded to the nearest integer.
